items.title: How Australians on JobSeeker are living on $68 a day
items.description: Despite calls to increase the base rate of JobSeeker payments in this year's federal budget, there has been no change and experts say it means the cost of living is hurting those who can least afford it.

items.title: 'I panicked': Developer tried to end affordable housing early
items.description: A property developer that describes itself as a leader in the national push to build cheap homes has been trying to scale back affordable housing at some of its projects.

items.title: Court says Meta must pay $806m for harming children's mental health
items.description: A New Mexico court has ordered Instagram and Facebook parent company Meta to pay $US567 million ($806 million) to address harms to young people from its platforms.

items.title: Men's behaviour change groups could soon face new rules
items.description: Programs range from one day sessions in schools educating boys on respectful relationships to months-long programs working with men who have abused their partners and children.

items.title: 'Extraordinary' Antarctic medevac performed in extreme -43C conditions
items.description: The temperature on the icy continent was a frosty -43 degrees Celsius when an Australian crew evacuated a polar expeditioner after an "urgent request for assistance".

items.title: Live: Marles denies cabinet divided on Burke's migration proposal
items.description: Richard Marles has denied cabinet was divided on the home affairs minister's proposal of sweeping cuts to migration. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Poll of economists expects RBA to leave cash rate unchanged
items.description: A poll of 37 of Australia's leading economists found all expect the RBA to leave its key cash rate unchanged after its meeting on Tuesday. Follow live.

items.title: After murder-suicide, police chief asks: 'Did we get it right?'
items.description: The actions of police in the lead-up to last week's murder-suicide involving a mother and her two young children will be considered as part of investigations, the state's police chief says.

items.title: First images show Moon's fresh crater after stray rocket impact
items.description: A South Korean satellite has captured the first pictures of the Moon's fresh crash scene caused by a stray SpaceX rocket, showing noticeably darker terrain.

items.title: As US burns through interceptors, Ukraine looks for backup elsewhere
items.description: Ukraine has reported that it could not defend itself against a recent barrage of ballistic missiles from Russia, which analysts say comes down to the US war with Iran.

items.title: Sea drones and explosive-laden robots to help de-mine Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Even with a range of high-tech equipment such as underwater drones and helicopter-mounted lasers, clearing the Strait of Hormuz of Iranian sea mine threats will be a painstaking and challenging process.

items.title: Australian councils swap grass for native wildflower meadows
items.description: You may have spotted more native plants popping up in your local park or on the side of the road. It's part of a push to create hardier, more beautiful council plantings across Australia.

items.title: Breaking: Show scraps bird and poultry exhibits amid rising H5 cases
items.description: Next month's Royal Adelaide Show will be without bird and poultry exhibits for 2026 amid the state recording the largest number of flu cases in the country.

items.title: Council decides to sell off farm donated 'in good faith' to community
items.description: Boyup Brook locals say they were blindsided by the shire's decision to sell off a beloved farm donated to the community more than four decades ago.

items.title: The affordable fresh fruit and veggies to shop for this month
items.description: From baby broccoli to gai lan, these are the vegetables (and fruit) to look for this month.

items.title: What happens when the world's largest online retail warehouse moves to town
items.description: Burra Creek is the home of the world's largest online retail warehouse. It's also the setting for a moving new production about the struggles faced by everyday Australian families.

items.title: Friday news quiz: A bored prince, Jetstar's new fee and a stunning view of … something
items.description: Please ensure your seat is upright and, if you can still afford it, stow your bag in the overhead compartment: this quiz is ready for take-off.

items.title: Athletes go missing after Commonwealth Games
items.description: Scottish Police are investigating after four members of the Ugandan boxing team reportedly failed to return home.

items.title: Toddler was rescued by police from scene of suspected murder-suicide
items.description: Murweh Shire Mayor Shaun Radnedge says the community will band together despite the devastating "violent" crime that has left a woman and a man dead.

items.title: Elizabeth Young wants the system that 'killed' her daughter fixed
items.description: The mother of a Bondi Junction stabbing victim has joined with six mental health organisations to pressure the NSW government for a better response to the April 2024 deaths of six people.

items.title: Broadcasting veteran Charlie King retires after 32 years with the ABC
items.description: After more than three decades with the ABC, sports commentator Charlie King is hanging up the headphones and heading into retirement.

items.title: 'Coded to Chinese': Hongkongers unable to list their ancestry on census night
items.description: People with Hong Kong heritage are frustrated that their ancestry will not be recognised as distinct from Chinese in the upcoming Australian census, despite years of lobbying and political turmoil.

items.title: Trump moves to ban 'birth tourism' and restrict birthright citizenship
items.description: An earlier effort by Mr Trump to roll back birthright citizenship was rejected by the US ‌Supreme Court in June, prompting him to ⁠call upon Congress to act on what has been one of the top priorities for his administration.

items.title: Prominent queer figure facing backlash for Geelong Liberal candidacy
items.description: One of Geelong's most prominent LGBTQIA+ figures is facing backlash from the queer community, after being announced as a Liberal candidate for the upcoming state election.

items.title: Australia wants lithium processed here but miners say numbers don't add up
items.description: Until recently, Australian lithium miners were digging up their ore and selling to China for processing into battery materials. Now, a handful of them are trying to get a bit more value out of that supply chain.
